newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Doctors approve Yeltsin operation, but see delay.
newsitem.headline: Doctors approve Yeltsin operation, but see delay.

text.p: Doctors decided on Wednesday to go ahead with a planned heart operation on President Boris Yeltsin, but said they would delay for six to eight weeks to increase his chances of surviving the surgery.
Russian cardiologist Renat Akchurin, expected to lead the operating team, told a news conference that the delay could boost Yeltsin's prospect of survival close to 100 percent.
"If we operate now, I would say the chance is about 80 percent, but we hope that in six weeks the percentage would be close to 100," Akchurin said.

The doctors, who met Yeltsin in Russia's exclusive Central Clinical Hospital, said that the 65-year-old Russian president needed an operation, but they were confident that he could return to a normal way of life.
"There is no reason why the president should not be restored to full, normal activity," pioneering U.S. heart surgeon Michael DeBakey told the briefing.

DeBakey, 23 years older than his new patient, helped developed the methods used in heart bypass surgery, in which an artery from the leg is grafted in to avoid a damaged blood vessel and improve the flow of blood to the patient's heart.
He was an adviser to the team of specialists who examined the president on Wednesday and decided when to operate.

DeBakey said he would be permanently available to return to Moscow to advise his Russian colleagues. U.S. President Bill Clinton had asked him to make it his "number one priority" and DeBakey said he had accepted Clinton's request.
DeBakey said it usually took people between six weeks and two months to recover from a heart bypass. Patients had a good chance of living for 10 years after surgery.
He said Yeltsin's liver and kidneys were working normally.

Yeltsin, 65, was re-elected on July 3 for a four-year term in the Kremlin. Opposition figures, including former Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev, have called on him to step down, complaining that he is too ill to rule.

The president, who had two heart attacks. has been in hospital since September 13 and Russian surgeon Andrei Vorobyov, the head of the council of doctors, he was likely to stay in hospital until the operation.

He said Yeltsin's heavy workload during the summer election campaign had "caused complications which make the operation undesirable today". He expected Yeltsin to work in hospital while doctors prepared him for the operation.
DeBakey stressed there was no problem with the president's mental faculties but he would be kept in hospital to monitor his health closely.
